one_liner: Senior supervisory contracting officer role advising Marine Corps leaders on major defense acquisitions, setting procurement policy, and managing a contracting staff.
fit_summary: This NH-4 role requires at least one year of GS-13/NH-03-equivalent specialized experience with expert knowledge of FAR/DFARS and Navy contracting policy, plus supervisory experience. Daniel's emergency-management consulting background at IEM is government-facing but not, as far as is known, hands-on federal contracting or procurement policy work. Unless Daniel's IEM role involved senior contract management and supervision, Daniel is unlikely to qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public, but this is a notice flyer for anticipated vacancies; you must follow the separate 'How to Apply' instructions, and there may be no actual hires.

At least one year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-13/NH-03, including expert knowledge of federal, DoD, and Navy contracting statutes, regulations, and contract types, plus supervising a staff.
Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution is required under the DoD GS-1102 standard; confirm you have one and keep transcripts ready.
Secret security clearance is required; you must be able to obtain and maintain it.
strategy: Be honest with yourself about whether your IEM work included real contract administration, proposal pricing, or procurement policy; if not, skip this posting and target GS-1102 entry or developmental roles (GS-7/9 Contract Specialist interns) or emergency-management and program roles.

If you did work on government contracts at IEM, frame it from the government-client side: contract types, task orders, cost and pricing, compliance with FAR clauses, and deliverables managed, with hours per week and dates.
Highlight any supervisory duties explicitly (staff count, assigning work, evaluations), since supervision is a mandatory specialized-experience element.
Showcase your communication strengths through concrete examples of briefing senior government officials or client leadership, which maps to the oral and written presentation requirement.
Keep the resume to two pages, mirror the posting's phrases, and submit by 11/30/2026 via the flyer's 'How to Apply' directions with transcripts attached.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] on [contract/task order type] valued at [$ amount], tracking deliverables, budgets, and compliance with [FAR/agency] requirements over [time period, hours/week].

Delivered [number] briefings to [senior government officials/client leadership] on [topic, e.g., recovery program status or procurement strategy], producing written recommendations adopted by [result if known].
Supervised [number] [professional/technical] staff, assigning work, setting priorities, and providing training to deliver [project] on schedule.
interview_questions: Describe a complex, high-value acquisition you managed and how you selected the contract type.
How have you analyzed cost and pricing data to reach a fair and reasonable price determination?
Tell us about a time you briefed senior leaders on a contentious contracting issue.
How do you handle a performance problem or complaint within your team?
watch_outs: This is a flyer for anticipated vacancies; no Notice of Result letters are sent, and there may be no hires.
Senior specialized contracting experience and supervision are hard requirements; an emergency-management consulting background alone is unlikely to qualify.
A bachelor's degree and Secret clearance are required.
